claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase fcc and hexagonal C14 Laves microstructure.
The fcc phase of FeCoNiTi has intrinsically limited orbital moments.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni analogs have coercivity capped near 100 Oe because of insufficient orbital moments and the absence of phase-boundary pinning.
The FeCoNiTi system has magnetic ordering transitions near 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K.
Controlling the C14 phase fraction and interfacial density can maximize fcc/C14 interfacial area.
Coexistence of the C14 phase can increase the coercivity of FeCoNiTi to approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
Antiferromagnetic exchange coupling develops between the Ti-rich C14 sublattice and the Fe/Co/Ni-rich fcc matrix.
Interfacial antiferromagnetic coupling reduces the net magnetic moment and saturation magnetization of the fcc phase.
Lattice mismatch and electronic discontinuity at fcc/C14 boundaries generate local magnetic anisotropy.
The fcc/C14 phase boundary acts as a domain-wall pinning site.
The C14 phase is a rigid, high-anisotropy pinning center.
Suppression of domain-wall motion by the C14 phase raises coercivity above the approximately 100 Oe single-phase limit.
In AlCoFeNi, partial substitution of Co by Cr promotes phase separation and increases coercivity.
In Cr-modified AlCoFeNi, the antiferromagnetic character of Cr reduces saturation magnetization by more than 50%.
Ti generally reduces magnetic moments in high-entropy alloys.
The dual-phase alloy will have lower saturation magnetization at 400 K than a single-phase fcc FeCoNiTi control because of spin compensation by the C14 phase.
If the C14 phase is strongly ferromagnetic and aligned with the fcc phase, it may increase saturation magnetization without producing the proposed coercivity enhancement through pinning.
Slower cooling or annealing can suppress C14 formation while retaining the same nominal FeCoNiTi composition.
A significant reduction in fcc spin density of states at the Fermi level at a C14 interface would indicate antiferromagnetic interfacial coupling.
